title: The coefficient-free twisted-path description of the Weil group
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], geometric Frobenius $\gamma:z\mapsto z^{1/q}$ and $g=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Let $X_0$ be geometrically connected, separated and of finite type over $k_0$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and choose a geometric point $b$ of $X$. Write $F_a$ for the finite-etale fibre functor at a geometric point $a$ [def-galois-fibre-functor]. A path $a\rightsquigarrow a'$ is a natural isomorphism $F_a\to F_{a'}$.

The set of pairs $(n,p)$, where $n\in\mathbf Z$ and $p:b\rightsquigarrow g^n b$, is a group with multiplication
$$(n,p)(m,q)=(n+m,g^m(p)\circ q).$$
Here $g^m(p)$ is the path obtained by applying $p$ to the pullbacks $(g^m)^*P$ of finite etale covers $P$. There is a degree-preserving group isomorphism from these pairs to $W(X_0,b)$ of [def-wf-weil-group], identifying $(0,p)$ with the geometric fundamental-group element $p$. On a finite etale $X_0$-cover $P_0$, the arithmetic action of $(n,p)$ is $p_{P_0\times_{k_0}k}$ followed by the canonical identification of the fibres at $g^n b$ and $b$ over the same geometric point of $X_0$. This characterizes the isomorphism.

Let $x$ be a closed point of $X_0$ with residue field $\kappa(x)$ of degree $e$ over $k_0$, choose a $k_0$-embedding $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow k$, and let $a:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ be its lift. Since $g^e a=a\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^e)$, reparametrization of lifted points defines a path
$$c_{a,e}:a\rightsquigarrow g^e a,\qquad z\longmapsto z\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^e)$$
on every finite etale cover. For every path $\tau:a\rightsquigarrow b$, the pair
$$(e,g^e(\tau)\circ c_{a,e}\circ\tau^{-1})$$
corresponds to the image of geometric Frobenius of $\kappa(x)$ under the decomposition-group map $\pi_1(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x))\to\pi_1(X_0,b)$ defined by $\tau$. Its degree is $e$. This statement concerns finite etale covers and paths only; it asserts no comparison of sheaf Frobenius operators.

source.place: Tags 0BND (pione-theorem-fundamental-group), 0BN5 (pione-lemma-functoriality-galois), 0BTV (pione-lemma-limit), 0BTX (pione-lemma-ses-field); Deligne, literature/deligne-weil-II_PMIHES-1980-52.pdf (1.1.7), (1.1.10)(ii), (1.1.12)-(1.1.13), pp. 150-153. Twisted-path formulas are an agent formulation of finite-cover fibre functors and constant-field descent.

proof.text: Write $\pi:X\to X_0$, $b_0=\pi b$, $F=F_b$ and $F_0=F_{b_0}$. By [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], $g$ is an automorphism over $X_0$. Pullback of finite etale covers and its natural fibre comparisons are [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] (or [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]). The fibre-product projections give $F_a((g^r)^*P)=F_{g^ra}(P)$ canonically: a lifted point is sent to its projection to $P$. For a path $u:a\rightsquigarrow a'$, define $g^r(u)_P=u_{(g^r)^*P}$ under these identifications. Associativity of fibre products gives $g^{r+s}(u)=g^r(g^s(u))$ and $g^r(v\circ u)=g^r(v)\circ g^r(u)$; both equalities are checked by projecting each lifted point to $P$.

source.place: Tags 0BN5 (lemma-functoriality-galois), 0BND (theorem-fundamental-group), 0BTX (lemma-ses-field); explicit agent-written fibre calculations. Deligne Weil II (1.1.7)-(1.1.8), (1.1.10)(ii), (1.1.13), pp. 150-153.

proof.text: The displayed multiplication is well typed: $q$ ends at $g^m b$ and $g^m(p)$ starts there. Both parenthesizations of three factors $(n,p),(m,q),(l,r)$ have degree $n+m+l$ and path $g^{m+l}(p)\circ g^l(q)\circ r$, by step 1. The identity is $(0,\mathrm{id}_{F_b})$ and the inverse of $(n,p)$ is $(-n,g^{-n}(p^{-1}))$; substitution gives the identity on either side. Thus the pairs form a group and projection to $\mathbf Z$ is a homomorphism. Its degree-zero subgroup is exactly $\operatorname{Aut}(F_b)=\pi_1(X,b)$ by [def-galois-fibre-functor].

source.place: Tags 0BN5 (lemma-functoriality-galois), 0BND (theorem-fundamental-group), 0BTX (lemma-ses-field); explicit agent-written fibre calculations. Deligne Weil II (1.1.7)-(1.1.8), (1.1.10)(ii), (1.1.13), pp. 150-153.

proof.text: For a geometric point $v$ of $X$, projection of lifted points identifies $F_v(\pi^*P_0)$ with $F_{\pi v}(P_0)$, naturally in finite etale $P_0\to X_0$, by [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality]. Since $\pi g^n=\pi$, denote the resulting identification between the fibres at $g^n v$ and $v$ by $r_{n,v,P_0}$. Set $A(n,p)_{P_0}=r_{n,b,P_0}\circ p_{\pi^*P_0}$. These are bijections natural for every arithmetic cover morphism, hence form an element of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_0)=\pi_1(X_0,b_0)$ [def-galois-fibre-functor]. In degree zero this construction is precisely the canonical map $i:\pi_1(X,b)\to\pi_1(X_0,b_0)$ of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality].

source.place: Tags 0BN5 (lemma-functoriality-galois), 0BND (theorem-fundamental-group), 0BTX (lemma-ses-field); explicit agent-written fibre calculations. Deligne Weil II (1.1.7)-(1.1.8), (1.1.10)(ii), (1.1.13), pp. 150-153.

proof.text: Write $b:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ and $\iota:k\hookrightarrow\Omega$ for its scalar map. Let $E/k_0$ be a finite subextension of $k$. It is separable and normal by [lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius]; $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is finite etale by [lem-sc-finite-etale-algebra-criterion], so its constant cover belongs to the category by [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. Each point of its fibre at $b_0$ is an embedding $E\to\Omega$. Normality says that every such embedding is $\iota\sigma$ for a $k_0$-embedding $\sigma:E\to k$: its elements satisfy polynomials already split in $\iota(E)$. The embedding $\sigma$ defines a section $s_\sigma:X\to X\times_{k_0}\operatorname{Spec}E$. Naturality of $p$ with respect to this section sends $s_\sigma b$ to $s_\sigma g^n b$, because the fibre of the identity cover $X$ is a singleton. After projection to the arithmetic cover this changes $\iota\sigma$ to $\iota\gamma^n\sigma$. Thus $A(n,p)$ acts on every constant field cover by $\gamma^n$. By [lem-wf-arithmetic-lift-fibre-path] (with $K=k_0$, $L=k$, $Y_0=X_0$, $\bar y=b$, $i=\iota$), the map $r:\pi_1(X_0,b_0)\to\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$ used in [def-wf-weil-group] is characterized by the action $\sigma\mapsto r(g)\circ\sigma$ on these constant covers, identified with their fibres through $\iota$. Hence $r(A(n,p))=\gamma^n$, and [def-wf-weil-group] puts $A(n,p)$ in $W(X_0,b)$ with degree $n$.

source.place: Tags 0BN5 (lemma-functoriality-galois), 0BND (theorem-fundamental-group), 0BTX (lemma-ses-field); explicit agent-written fibre calculations. Deligne Weil II (1.1.7)-(1.1.8), (1.1.10)(ii), (1.1.13), pp. 150-153.

proof.text:
For any descended cover $P=\pi^*P_0$, the isomorphism $(g^m)^*P\cong P$ is projection to the same $P_0$-coordinate. Naturality of $p$ for this cover isomorphism, with the identifications of step 3, reads
$$r_{n+m,b,P_0}\circ g^m(p)_P=A(n,p)_{P_0}\circ r_{m,b,P_0}.$$
Compose on the right with $q_P$. The result is $A(n+m,g^m(p)\circ q)=A(n,p)\circ A(m,q)$ on every arithmetic cover. Hence $A$ is a degree-preserving group homomorphism. On the degree-zero subgroup it is $i$ from step 3. By [lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence], this subgroup maps injectively onto $\ker(\deg:W\to\mathbf Z)$.

source.place: Tags 0BN5 (lemma-functoriality-galois), 0BND (theorem-fundamental-group), 0BTX (lemma-ses-field); explicit agent-written fibre calculations. Deligne Weil II (1.1.7)-(1.1.8), (1.1.10)(ii), (1.1.13), pp. 150-153.

proof.text: For each $n\in\mathbf Z$, surjectivity of degree in [lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence] supplies $s\in W$ with degree $n$. Apply [lem-wf-finite-etale-weil-transport] at $U_0=X_0$, $\bar u=b$: its pullback formulation gives a natural bijection $\lambda_{s,P}:F_b((g^n)^*P)\to F_b(P)$. Invert it and use the fibre comparison of step 1 to obtain a path $p_0:b\rightsquigarrow g^n b$. Only the asserted existence and all-morphism naturality of $\lambda_s$ are used; no normalization of its arithmetic action, and no construction from that node's proof, is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0BN5 (lemma-functoriality-galois), 0BND (theorem-fundamental-group), 0BTX (lemma-ses-field); explicit agent-written fibre calculations. Deligne Weil II (1.1.7)-(1.1.8), (1.1.10)(ii), (1.1.13), pp. 150-153.

proof.text: Fix $w\in W$ of degree $n$, and choose $p_0$ as in step 6. Then $A(n,p_0)^{-1}w$ has degree zero. By [lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence] it is $i(h)$ for a unique $h\in\pi_1(X,b)$. Steps 2 and 5 give $A(n,p_0\circ h)=A(n,p_0)i(h)=w$. This proves surjectivity. If $A(n,p)=A(n',p')$, degree preservation gives $n=n'$. Put $h=p^{-1}\circ p'\in\operatorname{Aut}(F_b)$. Then $p'=p\circ h$, so step 5 gives $i(h)=1$; injectivity of $i$ in the cited exact sequence gives $h=1$ and $p=p'$. Thus $A$ is the required isomorphism, with the specified geometric-subgroup identification. Its values on every arithmetic cover were prescribed in step 3; equality of natural automorphisms is equality of all components, so this prescription also proves uniqueness.

source.place: Tags 0BN5 (lemma-functoriality-galois), 0BND (theorem-fundamental-group), 0BTX (lemma-ses-field); explicit agent-written fibre calculations. Deligne Weil II (1.1.7)-(1.1.8), (1.1.10)(ii), (1.1.13), pp. 150-153.

proof.text: For the chosen closed point and embedding $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow k$, the finite-field Frobenius theorem [lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius] says that $\gamma^e$ fixes $\kappa(x)$: the $q$-power map has order $e$ on this field. On the $X_0$-coordinate, $a$ and $a\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^e)$ therefore agree; on the scalar coordinate both $g^e a$ and $a\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^e)$ equal $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^e)$. Hence $g^e a=a\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^e)$. If $z:\operatorname{Spec}k\to P$ is a lift of $a$, then $z\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^e)$ is a lift of $g^e a$. Reparametrization by $\gamma^{-e}$ is its inverse, and composition with any cover morphism commutes with this reparametrization. This constructs the path $c_{a,e}$ with exactly the formula in the statement.

source.place: Tags 0BN5 (lemma-functoriality-galois), 0BND (theorem-fundamental-group), 0BTX (lemma-ses-field); explicit agent-written fibre calculations. Deligne Weil II (1.1.7)-(1.1.8), (1.1.10)(ii), (1.1.13), pp. 150-153.

proof.text:
Restrict $\tau$ to descended covers and use projection to $P_0$ to obtain an arithmetic path $\tau_0:F_{\pi a}\to F_{b_0}$ [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality]. The definition of a decomposition-group map via $\tau_0$ sends $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/\kappa(x))$ to the automorphism with components $\tau_{0,P_0}\circ(z\mapsto z\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma))\circ\tau_{0,P_0}^{-1}$: this is restriction to the residue-field cover followed by change of fibre functor. For geometric Frobenius over $\kappa(x)$ take $\sigma=\gamma^e$, the inverse of the $q^e$-power map, by [lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius]. On descended covers, naturality of $\tau$ for $(g^e)^*\pi^*P_0\cong\pi^*P_0$ gives
$$r_{e,b,P_0}\circ g^e(\tau)_{\pi^*P_0}=\tau_{\pi^*P_0}\circ r_{e,a,P_0}.$$
Moreover $r_{e,a,P_0}\circ c_{a,e}$ projects to $z\mapsto z\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^e)$ on $P_0$. Substitute these two identities into step 3 for $p=g^e(\tau)\circ c_{a,e}\circ\tau^{-1}$. Its arithmetic action is exactly the above conjugate by $\tau_0$, on every $P_0$. It is therefore the stated decomposition-group image of geometric Frobenius. Its degree is $e$ by degree preservation. All comparisons here concern lifted points of finite etale covers.

Step 5: the homomorphism identity r_{n+m} g^m(p) = A(n,p) r_m. Step 7: the torsor bijectivity argument. Step 8: g^e a = a Spec(gamma^e). lean.note: The theorem asserts a Group on the actual pairs and an equivalence to the recorded Weil group, with the displayed multiplication and multiplicativity. Full arithmetic-cover components characterize the equivalence uniquely. Componentwise predicates include the geometric subgroup and residue-field return-path/decomposition formula. All helper data are explicit constructions; only the main theorem is postponed.
